reason: E3 confirms that high mixing entropy stabilizes simple lattices and that BCS pairing is supported. E1 and E2 indicate that electron count and disorder affect superconductivity, but neither directly demonstrates an optimal balance or isotropic s-wave gap from disorder alone; the specific claim of an optimum ΔSmix tuning Tc at fixed electron count is not directly evidenced.
premises: High mixing entropy stabilizes simple lattice structures (e.g., bcc) in HEAs
Superconductivity in HEAs is conventional BCS phonon-mediated with s-wave pairing
Electron count tunes the density of states at the Fermi level and affects Tc
Atomic-scale disorder (ΔSmix) influences superconducting properties such as Tc and gap characteristics
An optimal balance of disorder and electron count yields superconductivity; too much disorder can suppress it
